note: Which paths may legitimately differ between two installed devices, and what must be true of each one in the immutable artifact. This is NOT an exclusion list for the reproducibility comparison. A path here must be absent from the artifact (or present and empty, where that is declared), which the comparison can see; excluding it would mean the policy enforced nothing. release.mutablestate.policy_paths_are_not_excluded fails if any path here also appears in a comparison exclusion list, and a test holds that.

paths.reason: The BrlAPI authorisation key admits a client to the braille display daemon. brlapi's %post mints it with mcookie, so a container build bakes one key into the image and every device installed from that image shares it. It was one of the fifteen files that differed between two builders, which is how it was found.
paths.generationTime: first boot of the installed system, before brltty.service
paths.recoveryBehaviour: The unit's ConditionPathExists is negated rather than a first-boot stamp, so a key lost to a failed update, a restored backup or a recovery action is regenerated on the next boot. The failure mode of no key is no braille output, so absence must self-heal.
paths.securityRelevance: A shipped secret is a shipped secret. Removing it from the image is a strict improvement; generating it deterministically to make two builds match would satisfy the comparison and destroy the property the file exists for, and is refused.

paths.reason: systemd reads a zero-length machine-id as 'first boot, generate one'. Measured in the current artifact: present and 0 bytes, which is correct. It is recorded here because the comparison excludes it as a volatile path, so a build that wrote a real machine-id would not be detected by any dimension.
paths.generationTime: first boot of the installed system
paths.recoveryBehaviour: systemd regenerates it when absent or empty; no recovery action is needed.
paths.securityRelevance: A populated machine-id would give every installation the builder's identity, and D-Bus, systemd journal and several application-level identifiers derive from it.

paths.reason: Measured: Ubuntu's podman 4.9.3 writes the build container's hostname into the image and 5.8.4 does not. In the earlier hosted run this single file made filesystemTree, permissions and ownership all differ. It is the clearest evidence in this project that a hosted runner label is not a pinned environment.
paths.generator: the installer, or systemd's transient hostname on a device with none
paths.recoveryBehaviour: An absent /etc/hostname is valid; systemd falls back to the transient hostname.
paths.securityRelevance: Low on its own. It is builder-host identity leaking into a product artifact, which the mandatory principles forbid regardless of how little it reveals.

paths.reason: A host key shipped in an image is a private key every holder of that image possesses, and every device installed from it presents the same identity.
paths.generationTime: first start of sshd on the installed system
paths.recoveryBehaviour: sshd-keygen regenerates any missing key before sshd starts.
paths.securityRelevance: Shared host keys defeat host authentication entirely and make man-in-the-middle detection impossible across the fleet.

paths.reason: A second copy of the machine id, kept for compatibility. Shipping it would reintroduce the identity the empty /etc/machine-id exists to avoid.
A seed shared by every installation contributes no entropy and misrepresents how much the pool has.
paths.recoveryBehaviour: systemd creates it on the first clean shutdown; its absence is the normal state of a fresh installation.
paths.securityRelevance: A predictable early-boot entropy pool weakens every key generated before the pool is reseeded, including the BrlAPI key generated on the same boot.

paths.reason: Fedora's per-installation usage counter. Two of these differed between the builders. Contents measured as '0 0 345600 2': a bucket, an epoch and a count.
paths.generator: dnf, when it contacts a repository with countme enabled
paths.generationTime: never on a qualification build; countme=0 is written into every repository definition the image carries
paths.recoveryBehaviour: None required. The counter is telemetry and its absence changes no package operation.
paths.securityRelevance: It is behavioural reporting. Removing it matches the project's stated no-telemetry position; the change must not introduce any replacement reporting, and does not.

paths.reason: The package manager's own log, one wall-clock timestamp per line, written by the build's install and minimisation transactions. It differs between two builds of one commit by construction. It was the last dimension-invisible difference found: /var/log is excluded from the compared set as runtime state, which is right for a dimension and irrelevant to a layer tar, so it changed ociLayers and rawArchive while all fourteen content dimensions matched.
paths.generationTime: whenever the installed system runs a package transaction
paths.recoveryBehaviour: dnf5 recreates it on the next transaction. No history is lost that matters: what was installed is in the rpm database, and the transaction structure is in the libdnf5 history, both of which are retained.
paths.securityRelevance: It records when and where the artifact was built. That is builder-host identity leaking into a product artifact, which the mandatory principles exclude regardless of how little it reveals.

paths.reason: aux-cache stores an inode number, a size and two timestamps per shared object, and inode numbers are allocated by the filesystem the build happened to run on. Measured inside one layer at offset 47,478,304, two builds recorded different inode numbers for the same libraries. It also moved glibc's SPDX packageVerificationCode, which is what the sbom dimension was reporting.
paths.generationTime: whenever ldconfig runs on the installed system
paths.recoveryBehaviour: ldconfig regenerates it on demand; its absence costs one slower ldconfig run and changes no linking behaviour.
paths.securityRelevance: None directly. It is a filesystem-layout artefact of the build machine, and an inode number is not information a product artifact should carry.

paths.reason: A package cache is build residue. Build caches must not affect outputs and must not be shipped.
paths.generationTime: whenever the installed system fetches packages
paths.securityRelevance: A stale cache can serve superseded package metadata to a later transaction.

paths.reason: The libdnf5 half of the same cache, and the directory the resolution stage copies the transaction out of.
paths.generationTime: whenever the installed system fetches packages

paths.reason: Write-ahead-log residue, not state. It differed between the builders because it records where an unflushed transaction happened to stop. Checkpointing moves its contents into the database, where they belong.
paths.generationTime: during any package transaction on the installed system
paths.recoveryBehaviour: sqlite recreates the WAL on the next write; no data is lost by its absence after a checkpoint.
paths.securityRelevance: None. The transaction history itself is retained, because it supports repair, security auditing and licence inventory, and is not removed.

paths.reason: Shared-memory index for the WAL. Meaningless without it.
paths.generator: libdnf5, removed by build/scripts/finalise-image.sh after checkpointing
paths.generationTime: during any package transaction on the installed system
paths.recoveryBehaviour: Recreated by sqlite on the next open.
